schools.tuition_model: Per-credit, pay-as-you-go. Online undergraduate $354/credit for AY2026-27 (3-credit course = $1,062). No application fee; no separate course fee; e-texts generally included. Non-degree 'individual classes' allowed (up to 10 courses) with no transcripts, no diploma requirement, no test scores; federal financial aid NOT available to individual-course-only students. Six 8-week terms per year, register up to the day before a term starts.
schools.cost_basis_note: verified 2026-09 via indexed snippets of snhu.edu (direct page fetch was blocked by the sandbox egress proxy, so no page was opened in full). $354/credit is SNHU's stated AY2026-27 online undergraduate rate and is corroborated by SNHU's published BSBA total of $42,480/120 cr. NOTE: SNHU's own individual-class pages still advertise $1,026 per 3-credit course ($342/credit); if that is the rate actually charged the total falls to $4,104. The higher, more conservative $354/credit is used here. Course CODES and TITLES for PAD 330, PAD 345, CYB 200 and CYB 260 were each corroborated by two or more independent sources; PAD 345's prerequisite status and PAD availability to non-degree students are NOT verified.

courses.title: Cybersecurity Foundations
courses.notes: LOWER DIVISION (200-level). Foundational cybersecurity concepts; adversarial vs. environmental threats; explicitly covers legal and human factors and how they shape organisational security strategy. FULLY VERIFIED: SNHU sells this as a standalone individual class at snhu.edu/online-degrees/classes/cyber-security-foundations (8 weeks, 100% online, listed there at $1,026; priced here at the higher $354/cr rate). Prerequisites: NONE (verified). Required gate for CYB 260 - take this first.

courses.title: Legal and Human Factors of Cybersecurity
courses.notes: LOWER DIVISION (200-level) despite being the most policy-heavy course in the block: cybersecurity law and regulation, privacy/compliance, ethics, social engineering and human-factor attack surfaces. Code+title VERIFIED (Course Hero SNHU sitemap 'CYB 260 : Legal and Human Factors of Cybersecurity' + Studocu course page); indexed syllabus header lists 'Course Prerequisites: CYB 200'. This is the sharpest Technology-&-Government course SNHU offers and does not overlap UCLA Extension's power-electronics track.

schools.strengths_rationale: SNHU is the fleet's cheap, fast, regionally accredited (NECHE) supplier of APPLIED public-administration and cybersecurity-policy credit on a 6-per-year 8-week cadence with genuine no-strings non-degree enrolment (up to 10 courses, no transcripts, no diploma requirement, no application fee). It is the only one of the six platforms that runs a real undergraduate PAD teaching line (PAD 330/340/345/410, backing both a BSBA concentration and a standalone BA in Public Administration), and its CYB line has a zero-prerequisite 200-level entry plus a dedicated law/ethics/human-factors course. That combination lands exactly on the degree's 'Technology & Government' focus area while deliberately avoiding (a) UCLA Extension's power-electronics/grid engineering, (b) HES's theory-heavy policy and environmental science, and (c) UMPI's flat-rate bulk business/management, where marginal cost is effectively zero. QSO 340 Project Management - SNHU's signature applied course - was deliberately NOT selected because published syllabi gate it behind MAT 240 Applied Statistics and UMPI can deliver equivalent PM content inside its flat-rate block.
risks: PAD availability to non-degree students is UNVERIFIED: SNHU's individual-class menu (~500 courses) was confirmed to include CYB-200, QSO-340, IT-200 etc., but no individual-class page for PAD-330/PAD-345 was found. Fallback if PAD is concentration-only: QSO 340 Project Management (needs MAT 240 or a waiver) and/or COM 315 Communication in the Digital Age.

Prerequisite enforcement at registration: CYB 260 requires CYB 200, so the two must run in consecutive 8-week terms, not concurrently. Confirm with an admission counsellor that a non-degree student can register for a course whose prereq was completed at SNHU in the immediately preceding term.

Price uncertainty of about +/-$144 total: snhu.edu's tuition page implies $354/credit for AY2026-27 while snhu.edu's own individual-class pages still quote $1,026 per 3-credit course ($342/credit); secondary sources also disagree on the 2025-26 rate ($330 vs $342). The conservative $354 was used.

Only 6 of the 12 credits (PAD 330, PAD 345) are upper division; ASU's BA in General Studies requires 45 upper-division credits out of 120. If the 6-school fleet runs short on upper-division credit, swap CYB 200 + CYB 260 for PAD 340 Public Fiscal Management + PAD 410 (program development and evaluation) to make all 12 credits upper division.

No ASU equivalency is guaranteed: SNHU PAD/CYB courses will most likely post at ASU as elective or departmental credit rather than as named ASU equivalents. Acceptable for a General Studies BA whose focus areas draw on approved elective lists, but each course should be run through transferguide.apps.asu.edu / MyPath2ASU before payment.
Financial aid is unavailable to individual-course-only students, so all $4,248 is out-of-pocket cash.
The 2027-28 SNHU calendar is not yet published; the 2028 term dates in this file are pattern projections and must be re-validated before any Round-2 schedule relies on them.

schools.strengths_rationale: HES is the prestige/credibility slot, capped at 12 credits (8% of the 150.334-credit plan) but ~$6,780 of cash, and it buys three things no other platform in the fleet can produce. (1) Ladder Harvard faculty actually teaching the course: Dustin Tingley (Professor of Government, Harvard University) on the politics of the energy transition, and Mathias Risse (Berthold Beitz Professor in Human Rights, Global Affairs and Philosophy, Harvard Kennedy School) on the philosophy and ethics of technology and AI. SNHU, UMPI, BYU-IS and ASU ULC have no equivalent; UCLA Extension's strength is practitioner-taught engineering, not policy theory. (2) A real Government department (US politics, IR, comparative politics, political philosophy, public policy) -- the spine of the Technology & Government focus area. (3) A real ENVR department behind the Sustainability master's and the Environmental Policy & International Development certificate -- the law/regulatory layer that sits on top of UCLA Extension's power electronics and grid engineering. The division of labour is deliberate: UCLA supplies converters, inverters and grid integration; HES supplies the law, politics and ethics that decide whether any of it gets built. Open enrollment makes it accessible ('no application required'; 'you do not have to be an undergraduate student to take a course for undergraduate credit'), 4-credit courses hit the 12-credit quota in exactly 3 courses, and credit lands on a Harvard University transcript accredited by NECHE, which satisfies ASU's regionally-accredited + C-or-better transfer rule.
risks: COST: $565/credit is ~20x ASU ULC's effective rate. $6,780 for 12 credits is the single most expensive block per credit in the plan. This is a deliberate prestige purchase, not a savings play -- if the 20% cost-cutting objective ever outranks the 80% 'best of each school' objective, this is the first block to cut.

PACING: HES full terms are ~15 weeks and there are no 8-week or self-paced options for these courses. 12 HES credits realistically span TWO full terms across ~a calendar year (e.g. Spring 2027: PHIL E-150; Fall 2027: GOVT E-1722 + ENVR E-199). HES, not ULC or UMPI, is the pacing constraint on the whole 150.334-credit schedule. Round 2 must schedule around it first.
SCHEDULING: PHIL E-150 is observed only in the SPRING term and ENVR E-199 only in the FALL term. Only GOVT E-1722 has both-term flexibility. A missed spring costs a full year on PHIL E-150.

ENVR E-199 IS NOT FULLY VERIFIED. Code, title and CRN 17015 are confirmed; credit hours (4 assumed), undergraduate-credit availability, and delivery format are NOT. Verify on the live course page before registering. Documented fallbacks: ENVR E-119D Zero Energy and Passive Buildings (CRN 24776, verified code) or ENVR E-119E Sustainable Infrastructure (verified, but live Wednesday 5:30-7:30 PM sessions).

CREDIT LEVEL: must register at the UNDERGRADUATE (UN) credit level, not graduate. Same price, but HES graduate credit does not transfer cleanly into an ASU bachelor's. Easy and irreversible mistake at checkout.

TRANSFER GRANULARITY: expect elective / departmental transfer credit at ASU rather than a course-by-course Transfer Guide equivalency -- HES almost certainly has no pre-built ASU equivalencies. Fine for a BA in General Studies, but focus-area applicability needs an ASU advisor's written sign-off, ideally BEFORE paying $6,780.

GRADE FLOOR: ASU requires C- or better to transfer. Harvard grading in 4-credit full-term courses is demanding and these are reading/writing-heavy; budget real hours, especially in the term that carries two of them.
DOUBLE-COUNT EXCLUSION: GOVT E-1722 and GOVT S-1511 (the Harvard Summer School version) cannot both be counted. Do not let a summer-acceleration plan accidentally buy the same course twice.
